source.stem:
Multiple choice questions.

System of equations

$$
\left\{ \begin{array}{l} 3 x + 4 y = 5, \\ - 7 x + 9 y = - \frac {5}{2} \end{array} \right.
$$

The solution is ( ).

(A) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 2,\\ y = -0.25 \end{array} \right.$

(B) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -5.5,\\ y = 4 \end{array} \right.$

(C) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 1,\\ y = 0.5 \end{array} \right.$

(D) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -1,\\ y = -0.5 \end{array} \right.$

hinge.title: Decide whether a situation needs an exact number, a rounded-up value, a rounded-down value, or a nearest-place approximation.

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: Approximate value is the label that belongs on this item, so 'Decide whether a situation needs an exact number, a rounded-up value' is answered as approximate value rather than exact value.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: Approximate value is what produces exact value, so the usual direction of this relation is run backwards — on the item about Decide whether a situation needs an exact number, a.

mx.name: mechanism_conflation
mx.teacher_note: exact value is settled by running 'Decide whether a number such as one lakh is big or small only after': The same number can feel large in one context and ordinary in another; one lakh rice — on the item about Decide whether a situation needs an exact number, a.

intelligence.enrichment: Approximation is useful when exactness is unnecessary, but some contexts require exact numbers; rounding up gives a value above the actual number, rounding down gives a value below it, and nearest neighbours round to a chosen place value.
